title: Learning She's Crying for Me from the Triangle Band; Monk Brunies
summary: At sixteen or seventeen he heard Nick LaRocca then the Triangle Band; he recalls a cornetist's habits and Abbie Brunies' brother Monk.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: What about She's Crying for Me? Why did you ever pick that tune up?

Well when I was learning how to dance when I was about sixteen or seventeen, Nick LaRocka used to play up into Octavia with a guy named Wynn. And when they left, Sal Majada and Sam Majada, the Triangle Band, came in. And I could see old Sal was the trumpet. Sam and, what is Sal and Sam?
Tony was the trumpet. Tony, Tony.

Cornette Tony. The Cornette player had a bent mouthpiece because he'd hold his horn down. And he'd hold his handkerchief because he'd sweat, he wasn't coughing off a little. And he'd put the horn out the window. The bandstand was here and the window was here for the first tune. And the guy hit the cymbal, bang! And we used to call him Monk. Abbey Brunis, the drum player, his brother Moon, a monk, whatever you want to call him. He'd come over to my place and we'd reminisce about the old Octavia and he'd say,
Yeah, the Machado on the corner and stick it out the window.
What did you do to the down there? Bang! How about that? He'd make you laugh.
Abbey's drum brother. I said his brother.
I never did know him. Oh, he was a kid. He was a pretty great comedian. He knew all the old jazz tunes. He'd make fun of Better Than That's There. Yeah. Uncle Abbey.
Yeah, I don't remember. Uncle Abbey. He was a pretty great comedian.
No point in putting that down. I don't know.

I don't know his real name, but he was a kid. He'd always, usually brighten up my day when he'd come in, because as soon as he'd come in he'd hit on a desk. Let's have it. Da da da da da da da da da. That's the way he was.
Well, that was Henry was that guy, wasn't it? No, I remember.
It was Abbey Brunis, the drum player's brother. Yeah. I can't, we called him Monk. I remember him. We called him Monk. He had a big chin.
Joe Mraz calls him Moon. Yeah. We called him Monk.
